h1: Electrical Service and Meter Upgrades in Broward County
intro: Sometimes the problem is not one panel or one breaker, it is the whole electrical service showing its age. The mast is corroded, the meter socket is failing, the disconnect is tired, and patching one piece moves the trouble along. We rebuild the service entrance, the mast, meter socket, disconnect, grounding, and panel, for homes and commercial properties. We forecast the whole job and price it once before we begin.

definition.heading: What a service and meter upgrade is
definition.body: An electrical service and meter upgrade replaces the parts that bring power into your property, from the utility connection to the panel. That includes the mast and riser, the meter socket, the main disconnect, the grounding, and the panels. When enough of these have aged out, rebuilding them in one pass beats replacing them one at a time.

symptoms.title: Multiple parts of the service are failing
symptoms.body: It is not just the panel. The meter socket is worn, the disconnect is tired, and the panel is obsolete all at once, and upgrading the service as a whole is more honest than chasing one failure at a time.

symptoms.title: Your insurer wants the service updated
symptoms.body: A 4-point inspection or a carrier flagged the electrical service, not just the panel. Bringing the whole service to current code is what satisfies the inspection cleanly.

symptoms.title: The meter socket or mast is damaged
symptoms.body: The meter housing, the mast, or the point where power enters the building is corroded, loose, or scorched, or the utility red-tagged the meter. Damage at the front door of your electrical system often means the service behind it needs work too.

symptoms.title: The service is undersized for the property
symptoms.body: The building asks more of the service than it was built to give, and the panel is full with nowhere to grow. An undersized, maxed-out service is a candidate for an upgrade sized for how the property lives now.

benefits.title: The whole service, solved at once
benefits.body: Instead of chasing failures one at a time, you get an electrical service that is new, current, and working together, so the trouble does not migrate to the next tired piece.

localSections.heading: Aging services in South Florida housing
localSections.body: Broward County grew in waves across many decades, and each installed services built for the electrical life of its time. When we open an older service from West Palm Beach to North Miami Beach, the mast, meter socket, panel, and disconnect are often aging together, and salt air and heat corrode the whole assembly.

localSections.heading: How carriers view the electrical service
localSections.body: South Florida carriers scrutinize the electrical service, and their concern reaches beyond one obsolete panel. A 4-point inspection reports on the electrical system, so an aging or undersized service or an obsolete panel can fail the electrical section. A full upgrade brings everything to current code, and we pull the permit and meet the inspector so your carrier gets clean documentation.

guide.title: The complete guide to electrical service and meter upgrades in South Florida

sections.heading: What a service and meter upgrade is and when you need one
sections.body: Your electrical service is the path power takes from the utility to your circuits: the mast and riser, the meter socket, the main disconnect, the panels, and the grounding. An upgrade replaces that system, in whole or in the parts that have aged out. The full job is right when patching one piece costs more than rebuilding everything, up to current code and sized for the property.

sections.heading: When it is just the meter socket
sections.body: Sometimes the service is sound and the trouble is only the meter socket, the box holding the utility's meter. South Florida weather leaves it with rust, a cracked enclosure, scorch marks, or a crooked meter. Because the utility owns the meter, replacing the socket means a scheduled disconnect and reconnect, which we coordinate with the permit and inspection. If the utility red-tagged the meter, we manage it from start to finish.

sections.heading: How to choose a contractor for a job this size
sections.body: A service upgrade is one of the larger jobs you will authorize, so the contractor matters. Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor and a Broward County Master Electrician, with 286 permitted projects on public record. Our in-house crew rebuilds the service, pulls the permit, coordinates the utility, and meets the inspector, and we do not sell a full upgrade to a property that only needs a repair.

faqs.question: What exactly is included in a service and meter upgrade?
faqs.answer: It covers the electrical service as a system: the mast and riser, the meter socket, the main disconnect, the grounding, and the panels when they are part of the job. Rather than fixing one worn part and waiting for the next to fail, we bring the whole service up to current code, sized for how your property uses power today.

faqs.question: Can you just replace the meter socket, or does it have to be the whole service?
faqs.answer: We do both. If the service is otherwise sound and only the meter socket has failed, we replace the socket by itself and coordinate the utility disconnect, reconnect, and permit as one clean job. If we find the failure has spread to the disconnect or panel behind it, we will show you honestly what we see and let you decide.

faqs.question: Do I need a full upgrade, or just a repair?
faqs.answer: It depends on what we find, and we will tell you honestly. Many problems are a single repair or one part like the meter socket, and if that is what your property needs, that is what we recommend. A full upgrade makes sense when several parts are worn at once, when repeated repairs keep failing, or when an inspection flagged the whole electrical system.

faqs.question: How long will my power be off during the work?
faqs.answer: For part of the work, since replacing the service means interrupting the power that feeds it. We coordinate with the utility and tell you honestly ahead of time what to expect so you can plan around it. Because we run three trucks and staff the job with our own crew, it is a focused, in-and-out job rather than one that drags on.
